headline: Wall Street plummets in the final hour of trading as the Federal Reserve delivers its first interest rate hike in three years and signals a hawkish outlook with further tightening planned. U.S. stocks sold off sharply on Wednesday afternoon after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted unanimously to raise the benchmark federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a new target range of 3.75% to 4.00%. While the immediate rate increase was widely expected by futures markets, stocks collapsed from their midday highs during Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference. The central bank took a decisively aggressive stance, upwardly revising economic growth projections while confirming that inflation remains elevated enough to justify one or two additional rate hikes before the end of the year.

headline: Wall Street slides for the sixth time in seven sessions as soaring energy costs and a relentless climb in bond yields compound corporate execution anxieties ahead of the Federal Reserve interest rate decision. U.S. stock indices closed cleanly lower on Tuesday as macroeconomic and fixed-income variables continued to dial up systematic pressure on broad valuations. Ongoing supply constraints related to key global crude line restrictions pushed Brent crude contracts up another 2.9% to close near $108.75 a barrel, stoking deep structural core inflation fears. In response, the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield spiked above 5.04% intraday—marking its highest structural level since 2007—before finishing the session near the 5.00% mark. The bond move forced rapid institutional re-weighting, sending capital out of credit-sensitive and high-multiple consumer spaces while raising the CME FedWatch probability of a central bank rate hike to 94%.
